dimensions.assessment: The legislation directly affects the members of the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe and relevant federal land management agencies.
dimensions.evidence: for the benefit of the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe

dimensions.assessment: It changes land status to trust ownership for the tribe and places specific management and gaming restrictions on those acres.
dimensions.evidence: takes approximately 1,082.63 acres of specified lands in Washington into trust

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not specify exact federal appropriations or economic impacts, beyond requiring a boundary survey.
It alters land designation for a specific geographic tract and places statutory restrictions on gaming and river management.
dimensions.evidence: prohibits gaming on the land taken into trust

dimensions.assessment: Placing land into trust and adding it to the reservation creates permanent status changes.
dimensions.evidence: Land taken into trust shall be part of the tribe's reservation.

missing_information: Specific cost estimates or appropriations for conducting the land survey.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill transfers approximately 1,082.63 acres of federal land into trust for the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe in Washington, adds the land to their reservation, manages a portion under the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act, and prohibits gaming on the trust lands.
